newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares power ahead in dollar-led surge.
newsitem.headline: German shares power ahead in dollar-led surge.

text.p: The seemingly unstoppable German share market soared further on Monday, as the strong dollar propelled the blue chip DAX past yet another psychologically crucial level -- 4,100 points.
Export shares and heavyweight insurance stocks led an advance that sent the DAX to a high of 4,119.84 points in the first half hour of trade, some 55 points above its old record.
The 30-share index was trading up 73.20 points, or 1.8 percent, at 4,114.17 points at 0903 GMT.
"This doesn't surprise me in the least," said one Frankfurt trader. "It's totally justified at this dollar level. There is not a single weak signal out there."
The dollar was holding at a six-year high of more than 1.78 marks -- providing further grounds for optimism for Germany's largely export-driven corporate earnings.
Chemical companies Hoechst, Bayer and BASF were trading heavily and firmly keeping up with overall market gains.
Hoechst was up 1.20 marks at 70.75 marks, Bayer up 1.30 at 73.75 and BASF up 88 pfennigs at 67.85 marks.
Electronics and engineering giant Siemens, continuing a spate of popularity, was up 2.25 marks at 114.85.

Insurance shares were surging, boosted by news earlier this month of a merger creating Germany's second largest primary insurer, combined with a better than expected earnings report on Friday from reinsurer Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG.
Munich Re, whose earnings per share rose to a record 150 marks for 1996/1997, was trading at record levels, and was up 375 marks, or more than six percent, at 6,325 marks.
Allianz AG, which owns 25 percent of Munich Re, was up 18.50 marks, or 4.5 percent, at 434.50 marks.
